model: STRIDE-per-element threat model of the round-1 slice of sgit-ai 0.21.0
method: mrwadams/mcp-stride-gpt skills/stride-threat-modelling (pinned in review/tools/skills.lock.json), run by the sgit-ai CLI agent on 2026-10-11 with no model API key and no hosted MCP: steps 1 (scope), 2 (enumerate per element, all six categories, N/A recorded), 3 (DREAD), 4 (mitigations as register references), 7 (coverage). Attack trees and Gherkin tests are not produced here: the register's tests/security suite is the test plan.

inputs.system_description: review/intent/*.json (assets, actors, boundaries, mechanisms from the threat model §2-§5)
inputs.app_type: CLI tool (Python) talking to a zero-knowledge object store over HTTPS; a static-file transport; local key stores
inputs.authentication: a bearer write key checked by the host (no cryptographic role); read access is possession of a symmetric read key; commits are ECDSA-signed by per-clone keys trusted because their key file decrypts under the read key
inputs.internet_facing: the host is; the CLI is not a server in this slice (serve/mirror/publish are round 2)
inputs.sensitive_data: vault key, read key, write key, access token, clone signing keys, file content and names, history integrity

dread_note: Affected Users is scored per vault (the users of one vault), not across all sgit users; Discoverability assumes the attacker reads this public repository.

elements.name: host store: content-addressed objects; mutable refs, branch index, key files
.sg_vault/local: vault_key, token, base_url, *.pem, clone_mode.json, remote config, remote_heads.json
~/.sg-send: vaults.enc credential store, pki keys, keyring
push: machine → host, including presigned multipart PUT
checkout / revert / switch / stash pop / restore: vault data → working copy
commit / write: working copy → vault data
argv, environment, stdout, stderr: operator or agent ↔ process
static transport: static host or local folder → machine (Vault__API__Static)
A3 read-key holder, A4 teammate, A8 other clients
A9 the agent holding the key

threats.title: A read-key holder with store access authors commits, refs, index entries and key files every client accepts as genuine, because signing keys are trusted when their file decrypts under the read key
threats.why: complete history forgery for one vault; deterministic once the attacker has the read key and a write path; needs the host or a mirror (M in the register) which is why the register ranks likelihood M
threats.mitigation: owner-signed membership of signer keys (register §6.4), pinned on clone

threats.title: a teammate signs a commit that claims another branch_id (signer not bound to branch)
threats.mitigation: bind branch_id into the signed form

threats.title: the host substitutes object bytes
threats.status: mitigated: verify-before-write on every download path
threats.mitigation: content address checked before any write (M2)

threats.title: the host serves one mutable file's ciphertext under another id (ref swap, key-file swap): no associated data binds a mutable file to its id
threats.mitigation: AES-GCM AAD = file id (format bump) or a writer-signed index

threats.title: the host replays an older index and drops features / min_client for existing clones
two clones push the same new branch at once and overwrite each other (no create-if-absent on the API)
a write-key holder deletes or rewrites history on the host and denies it; the host keeps no plaintext log and the write key names no writer
threats.mitigation: clones and backups recover; rewind guard tells clones; per-writer authorisation is a server design item (10/08 review)

threats.title: tag deletes (tombstones) are unsigned, so a read-key holder with store access can delete a tag and nothing attributes it

the host (and the network on https) sees exact plaintext sizes, object counts, change timing, team size and the vault id; deterministic tree encryption leaks equality of names and sizes across commits
threats.why: always on and public; damage is metadata only, which keeps D at 4 while the other four factors max out

threats.title: read access cannot be revoked: a read key reads all history forever, and a rekeyed vault leaves the old one readable until deleted
threats.mitigation: delete the old vault after rekey

threats.title: a vault created before 10/09 still carries its named branch's private signing key encrypted under the read key
threats.status: fixed for new vaults 0.21.0 (TM-R02); accepted for older vaults until moved (TM-R27)

threats.title: the host withholds objects or refs
threats.why: trivially available to the host; the damage is availability only and clones keep working offline
threats.status: mitigated for integrity (clone refuses an incomplete HEAD), accepted for availability

threats.title: the host swaps two key files so every signature fails (verify DoS)
every write-key holder has every write: no per-writer authorisation, no per-branch permission
threats.mitigation: server-side per-writer keys or signed writes the server verifies

threats.title: a forged (self-signed) head is pulled and `check verify` calls it verified
a clone with a withheld or substituted HEAD blob reads the file as deleted and the newcomer's next commit deletes it for everyone
a local ref, baseline or policy is written from server data before the check that should gate it (verify-then-accept ordering)
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (Vault__Incoming_Check: one rule); residual: the 21 swallowed exceptions on this path are BA-007 in review/findings/bandit.json, to be checked against the verify-group dossier

threats.title: the host serves a garbled branch index to a newcomer; the clone degrades to a synthesised index with no features and runs without signatures-required
threats.status: fixed this round for present-but-unreadable (TM-F35); the withheld-index variant stays accepted under TM-R29

threats.title: the host moves a branch backwards (rollback) for a fresh clone, which has nothing to compare with
threats.status: mitigated for existing clones (rewind guard, read-only included since 10/09); accepted for fresh clones
threats.mitigation: a freshness anchor (SP-2) or a signed head

threats.title: a tag entry another client wrote in a shape this build cannot read is dropped on the next index write, or a deleted tag comes back
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (entries carried unchanged); version-skew residuals accepted; the whole-index twin (an index this build cannot parse overwritten by the pushing clone) fixed this round, TM-F36

threats.title: an unsigned or no-key commit arrives under signatures-required and is accepted because the policy start cannot be read
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (fails closed); pre-0.21 vaults have no recorded start (accepted)
threats.mitigation: re-enable the policy once to record a start

threats.title: a vault whose server is http:// sends the token, the write key header and ciphertext in clear; the CLI warns only when a private key is used
threats.why: opt-in and warned, which the register uses to rank likelihood L; DREAD does not score likelihood
threats.mitigation: default is https; SE-004 proposes the same warning for a saved --no-verify-tls

threats.title: a remote saved with --no-verify-tls makes every later command accept any certificate, silently
hostile tree shapes (very deep, shared subtrees) make flatten slow or recurse deeply
a presigned URL from the host points at file://, data:, ftp:// or an internal http host and the client follows it
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (https, or http to loopback or the vault's own host; timeout 300 s)

threats.title: the host reports a lost compare-and-swap as success (HTTP 200 with a per-op conflict) and the client believes it pushed
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0; an EMPTY reply counted as pushed until TM-F33 (this round)

threats.title: a lost index CAS race uploads an unmerged index and drops signatures-required
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (index merge/CAS failure fails the push)

threats.title: a push from a clone with no signing key lands unsigned under the policy and nothing says so
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (warns; move and restore carry the .pem)

threats.title: SGIT_DEFAULT_BASE_URL (or a planted base_url file) redirects the token, the write key and the data to another host
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (server pinned per vault and per command; the variable on an unrecorded vault refuses)

threats.title: --debug prints presigned URL query strings (X-Amz-Credential, possibly X-Amz-Signature) to stderr
push --force without a lease overwrites a teammate's work; a status refresh used to move the lease baseline
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (one baseline per named branch, moved only by guarded operations; --force-with-lease)

threats.title: the host lists no files (or omits the named ref) and a clone that has already synced takes it for a first push, plain-writing its stale refs over the host's: the shared branch rewinds under a legitimate key
threats.status: fixed this round (TM-F34); found by the host-boundary dossier and reproduced
threats.mitigation: a clone with a baseline refuses an empty or ref-less listing

threats.title: the write key is one bearer secret per vault: any holder may delete everything on the host

vault data writes outside the tree or into .git / .sg_vault (any spelling: case, 8.3, NTFS streams, ignorable code points) through revert, switch, stash pop, sparse, restore, delete-on-pull, sgit write
a write through a symlink in the working copy lands outside the tree; a tracked path replaced by a link is written through
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (links never followed or written through)

threats.title: a planted .vault__*.zip or a hostile backup member is restored by init --restore / extractall outside the store
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (restore extracts store members only; structural backup name)

threats.reason: checkout writes files; no identity is asserted on this flow beyond the commit signature already covered under E7
local writes are the user's own; the reflog (local, capped) records ref moves (TM §git mapping)
plaintext lands in the user's own working copy by definition

threats.title: writes to a FIFO or device at a tracked path block revert/switch
threats.mitigation: lstat before open, as read_regular now does

threats.title: a secret in the working copy is committed and pushed: a vault-key backup zip, a hard link to .sg_vault/local/vault_key, an in-tree symlink to a key, a tracked .env
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 for zips, hard links and links; tracked-wins .env accepted; plain copies of key text accepted (TM-R34)
threats.mitigation: M11; keys never living in the working tree is the defence

threats.title: a file sgit cannot open is committed as deleted (permission denied, EIO, a file held open on Windows, an unlistable folder)
a commit is made with a key that is not the clone's own (a planted .pem) and verifies as that clone

threats.reason: every commit is signed by the clone key and carries author_key_id (0.19.0+); repudiation here is ST-E2-S1

threats.title: a catastrophic --grep pattern makes history log slow (no regex timeout)
threats.mitigation: pattern guard exists; residual overlap alternation

threats.reason: commit cannot grant any capability; the write happens at push (E8)

threats.title: a key-bearing file is created world-readable, or written then chmod'ed with a readable window, or written through a link
.sg_vault/local is 0755 (file names visible); a read-only clone keeps its read key on disk in clone_mode.json; the clone signing .pem is unencrypted at 0600
the vault-path type rewrites characters outside its class to '_', splitting the local store between the real root and a sanitised one (uninit and backups miss it; two roots can share one)
threats.status: reproduced (AC-L-001); fix soon, a decision on the type
threats.mitigation: validate the root once, never rewrite it

threats.title: a corrupt or deleted remote_heads.json read as empty, so the next pull accepts a rewind
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (fails closed, atomic write with fsync)

threats.reason: no identity is asserted by the store itself; a planted .pem is ST-E10-S1
local store, the user's own

threats.title: a planted pip.py or a hostile cwd affects `sgit update`

threats.reason: possession of the files is the privilege; covered by ST-E3-I1/I2

threats.title: `sgit pki delete <fingerprint>` joins an unvalidated argv string into a path and rmtree's it: `..` empties ~/.sg-send including vaults.enc
threats.status: fixed this round (TM-F32); found by the sharp-edges pass
threats.mitigation: validate the fingerprint shape in the stores; refuse a path outside keys_dir

threats.title: the credential store derives its master key with one fixed global salt: equal passphrases give equal keys on every machine (precomputation across users)
`sgit pki export ../x` reads a PEM from an arbitrary folder
a signed-then-encrypted PKI message can be re-wrapped for a third party with the original signature intact (no recipient binding)
threats.mitigation: v3 payload signing recipient + w + i + c

threats.reason: local store
destruction is ST-E6-T1
no privilege boundary inside the user's home

threats.title: keys on the command line (argv, shell history, process listings) and printed by init, create, vault info; an agent's transcript or a CI log captures them
threats.why: re-ranked High in the register on 10/09 for the same reason: agents' command lines and logs are read by many tools
threats.status: accepted; PKI phase 2 (wrapped capabilities) removes most of it
threats.mitigation: key prompts exist; the skill rule (step 5) forbids echoing keys

threats.title: an environment variable changes which server a vault talks to
a credential pasted into the wrong slot is routed by shape: a 64-hex passphrase was once read as a read key and sent a vault to a read-only clone
threats.status: mitigated by declared prefixes (classify_key); the bare shorthand remains documented (SE-006)

threats.reason: the operator's own shell
self-DoS only (ST-E10-D1)
the process runs as the user; nothing elevates

threats.title: a static host serves an old but authentic ref: no freshness anchor; the manifest is the authority for the two consumers that cannot fall back; whole-site substitution
threats.status: accepted (SP-2, SP-3, SP-14); serve/mirror/publish are round 2

threats.title: a file id from the vault's own index carries '..' or a scheme into the static location and urlopen/open follows it
threats.status: VERIFY (SG-004): the docstring says traversal returns None; to be traced in step 4

threats.reason: same as E7: content addressing and signatures; no further identity
read-only transport

threats.title: a private read key reaches the static host through a URL fragment or an http:// clone

threats.reason: availability of a static mirror is the host's; clones keep working

threats.title: `sgit update` installs the latest sgit-ai unpinned; no dependency audit or static-analysis gate in CI; no lockfile
threats.status: accepted; this review adds the baseline gate (step 3) and recommends a lockfile
threats.mitigation: M15 plus pip-audit, Bandit, Semgrep in the security job

threats.reason: release actions are SHA-pinned and PyPI publishing uses OIDC (gha review, cleared)
out of this slice
no secrets reach CI beyond the Docker Hub token in the main-only publish job (gha review)
out of this slice

threats.title: the CI token runs with the repository's default permissions (no workflow-level permissions: block)
threats.status: new, outside the external-attacker model (gha review note 7)
threats.mitigation: permissions: contents: read at the top; elevate per job

threats.title: the agent mints or borrows a signing key and commits as another clone, or forges commit metadata (insider S1, S2, R3)
threats.status: by design: an agent with the vault key is a teammate (A4); attribution is per clone key, not per agent
threats.mitigation: one clone and one .pem per agent; owner-signed membership would make minting visible

threats.title: the agent reads .sg_vault/local/vault_key or runs `vault info` and the key lands in its transcript, a log or another tool (insider S1, I4, I5)
threats.status: accepted today; the skill rule (step 5) and PKI phase 2 are the controls

threats.title: the agent destroys local state through its own commands: `pki delete ..` (ST-E6-T1), `push --force`, `vault uninit`, a wrong `revert` (insider D4)
threats.status: partly mitigated (lease, rewind guard, structural backup names); ST-E6-T1 is new
threats.mitigation: validate every argv path; keep destructive commands behind explicit flags

threats.title: the agent interleaves a harmful commit among legitimate ones in a long session; sgit attributes to the clone key, not to the task (insider R2)
threats.mitigation: commit messages carry the task id; reflog is local

threats.title: the agent floods the host with pushes or clones (insider D1, D3)
threats.status: host-side rate limiting is the control; out of the CLI

threats.title: the agent uses the one write key beyond its task: deletes the vault, rewrites history, switches signatures-required off (insider E2)
threats.mitigation: per-writer authorisation on the server; scoped tokens (PKI phase 2)

threats.title: a newcomer clones an unsigned head silently because clone (and clone-branch / clone-range) skipped signatures-required
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (every clone workflow runs verify-signatures before any write)
threats.added: second pass, after the join showed the rows unnamed

threats.title: a far-future tag entry or tombstone pins a name forever; `resolve` follows an unverified tag; a signed 4–6 hex tag is shadowed by any commit whose id starts the same way (minable)
threats.status: fixed 0.21.0 (far-future loses; resolve requires verified; ambiguous names refused)

threats.title: 48-bit object ids on format 1: a crafted collision is an error, never an overwrite, but the id space is small
a user-chosen passphrase is not strength-checked; the PBKDF2 cache keeps derived keys in process memory
other clients (the web UI, older sgit) ignore client-side policy: format gate and signatures-required are not enforced by them
threats.status: by design; min_client keeps old sgit out of writes

threats.reason: the process itself is modelled through its flows (E7–E12) and stores (E3–E6); nothing is left that is not one of those
.sg_vault/bare is a local copy of E2 under the same keys; its threats are E2's (substitution is verified on the way in, E7) and E3's (file modes)
the working copy's threats are the two flows that cross it, E9 and E10
external entities are the actors of the threats above; they carry no threats of their own
